original_idea.body:
# Refusal-Direction Drift Across Conversation Turns

Extract the refusal direction at turn 1, then track the projection of harmful-request activations onto it across a multi-turn escalation dialogue to test whether the refusal signal erodes turn-by-turn. Inference-only activation extraction on one consumer GPU (Arditi et al., NeurIPS 2024).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — mechanistically explaining multi-turn jailbreak success (the dominant attack regime) connects interpretability to a real threat.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: extract a refusal direction and track its projection across turns; activation extraction needs ML fundamentals but inherited methodology exists.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped single experiment (refusal-direction projection vs turn) with clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: one open model, inference-only activation extraction, no internal access, weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + activation extraction on one open model, single consumer GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Refusal-direction behavior across conversation turns is noted as unstudied.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Multi-turn refusal-direction drift explicitly noted as unstudied.
